# Sacubitril/Valsartan in Heart Failure: A Narrative Review

## Introduction

Heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare expenditure worldwide, affecting an estimated 64 million people [1]. For decades, neurohormonal blockade with angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists formed the cornerstone of treatment for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) [2]. The advent of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition (ARNI), embodied by the first-in-class agent sacubitril/valsartan, marked a paradigm shift in pharmacotherapy [3].

## Pharmacology and Rationale

Neprilysin is an endopeptidase that degrades several vasoactive peptides, including natriuretic peptides, bradykinin, and adrenomedullin [4]. Inhibition of neprilysin augments natriuretic peptide activity, promoting natriuresis, vasodilation, and inhibition of pathological remodeling [5]. However, neprilysin inhibition alone also raises angiotensin II, so combination with angiotensin receptor blockade is required to achieve net benefit [6]. Sacubitril/valsartan is a supramolecular sodium salt complex combining the neprilysin inhibitor prodrug sacubitril (AHU377) with the angiotensin receptor blocker valsartan [7]. Early efforts to combine neprilysin inhibition with ACE inhibition (omapatrilat) were abandoned because of an unacceptable incidence of angioedema attributable to dual bradykinin accumulation [8].

## Pivotal Clinical Evidence in HFrEF

The landmark PARADIGM-HF trial randomized 8,442 patients with NYHA class II–IV HFrEF to sacubitril/valsartan or enalapril [3]. The trial was stopped early for benefit; sacubitril/valsartan reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization by 20%, with significant reductions in all-cause mortality [3]. Subsequent analyses demonstrated reductions in sudden cardiac death and improvements in symptoms and quality of life [9,10]. The PIONEER-HF trial extended these findings to patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF, showing greater reductions in NT-proBNP compared with enalapril when initiated in-hospital after hemodynamic stabilization [11]. The TRANSITION trial confirmed feasibility and tolerability of in-hospital initiation [12]. These data prompted guideline committees to recommend ARNI as a foundational therapy, increasingly favored over ACE inhibitors or ARBs as initial therapy [13,14].

## Mechanistic and Biomarker Insights

Sacubitril/valsartan promotes reverse cardiac remodeling. The PROVE-HF study demonstrated that reductions in NT-proBNP correlated with improvements in left ventricular ejection fraction, volumes, and filling pressures over 12 months [15]. The EVALUATE-HF trial showed favorable effects on aortic stiffness and cardiac structure [16]. Effects on biomarkers of collagen turnover and myocardial fibrosis have also been reported [17]. Notably, sacubitril/valsartan raises circulating BNP (a neprilysin substrate) while lowering NT-proBNP (which is not), an important consideration in biomarker interpretation [18].

## Heart Failure with Preserved and Mildly Reduced EF

The PARAGON-HF trial evaluated sacubitril/valsartan in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and narrowly missed its primary endpoint (rate ratio 0.87; P = 0.06) [19]. Prespecified subgroup analyses suggested benefit among patients with ejection fraction below the median and in women [20]. A pooled analysis of PARADIGM-HF and PARAGON-HF suggested benefit extending into the mildly reduced and lower-preserved EF ranges [21]. These findings informed broadened regulatory labeling and guideline recommendations for selected patients with HF and EF below normal [14].

## Safety and Tolerability

In clinical trials, sacubitril/valsartan was associated with more hypotension but less hyperkalemia and renal impairment compared with enalapril [3,22]. Angioedema occurred infrequently, and a mandatory 36-hour washout is required when switching from an ACE inhibitor to avoid overlapping bradykinin effects [3]. Theoretical concerns regarding neprilysin inhibition and amyloid-beta accumulation have not translated into demonstrable cognitive harm in the PERSPECTIVE trial [23]. Real-world registries have broadly confirmed the safety and effectiveness observed in trials [24,25].

## Special Populations and Implementation

Benefits appear consistent across age, sex, diabetes status, and renal function strata [26]. Sacubitril/valsartan can be safely combined with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors as part of contemporary quadruple therapy [27]. Cost-effectiveness analyses generally support its use within accepted thresholds in HFrEF [28]. Despite robust evidence, underutilization and suboptimal dose titration persist, driven by cost, inertia, and tolerability concerns [29]. Quality-improvement initiatives and simplified initiation algorithms have improved uptake [30].

## Conclusion

Sacubitril/valsartan represents a transformative therapy for HFrEF, with mortality and morbidity benefits exceeding those of conventional renin-angiotensin blockade, and emerging though more modest benefit in patients with HF and below-normal ejection fraction [3,19,21]. Ongoing efforts should focus on equitable implementation, optimal sequencing within quadruple therapy, and further defining its role across the EF spectrum [14,30].
